assumptions.evidence: Arbitrary normalized balance sheets and transaction sizes selected to expose monetary mechanisms. No observed or forecast monetary stock, currency regime, market price or credit capacity is asserted.
assumptions.opening_boundary: Earth and array counterparties aggregate external customers, suppliers and investors. The S issuer is assigned to Earth for this example only, with an explicit 225 S claim on the Earth counterparty matching its 225 S liabilities. This is a closed accounting boundary, not a proposed Earth banking system or a forecast of reserve-currency dominance. Bank net worth is unallocated capital; shareholder equity securities, price risk, accrued interest, collateral encumbrance and regulation are outside the ledger.
assumptions.policy_boundary: Collateral limits and solvency checks are illustrative access rules, not calibrated regulatory standards. The additional post-insolvency loan is an explicit accounting counterfactual, not an eligible operation or recommendation. Foreign liquidity examples assume the quoted exchange rate remains available; they do not establish a credible peg or an endogenous floating rate. All scenarios restart from the same opening balance sheets.
assumptions.real_asset_boundary: The Earth counterparty holds movable produced equipment physically located on Earth. The import transaction explicitly transfers both its economic ownership and its location to Moon firms at the same fixed U value. It is not a purchase of land, a security or equipment remaining on Earth. Freight and transaction costs are outside the example. Initial lunar real assets are produced capital. The domestic damage event is an assumed destruction of produced capital, classified as an other-volume change, not a payment or recurring depreciation estimate.
assumptions.units: Amounts are normalized currency units. L is a hypothetical lunar contract currency; S is a hypothetical externally issued settlement currency. U is only the common valuation numeraire and is not issued money. No conversion to the mature world-economy product is defined.

boundaries: No GWP/NWP baseline or existing economic product is changed.
Accounting consistency is not evidence of sustainable fiscal or monetary policy.
No exchange-rate equilibrium, inflation, credit demand, interest-rate response, default probability, regulatory capital rule or liquidity-premium forecast is made.
Money creation, real resources, liquidity, solvency and financing capacity require separate evidence.

domestic_liquidity_and_solvency.boundary: Current transfers isolate settlement. No production is inferred. Assumed capital damage reduces real wealth before debt forgiveness. Agreed debt cancellation is a capital transfer that legally releases the borrower; it is not an impairment provision. Last credit is an expressly ineligible accounting counterfactual.

external_debt_denomination.boundary: External purchase is assumed, not predicted. Borrowing creates a financial inflow and external liability; it is not export income. Funds retained in the lunar CB remain an external asset. Local fiscal transfers create no current-account entry. Contract face is unchanged by imposed L depreciation. No foreign creditor loss/repricing response, hedging or inflation response is modeled.

foreign_settlement.boundary: Earth delivers existing movable produced equipment to the Moon and transfers economic ownership; array consumes a lunar service. Costs, value added, freight limits and prices are not modeled. No foreign debt/interest/current transfers/capital transfers occur in this sequence. External receipt first belongs to the bank, not the CB. Depreciation is imposed after settlement, with fixed U real-asset values and no behavioural feedback; its NFA effect is zero here because cross-border claims are all S-denominated.

treasury_and_central_bank.boundary: The unconditional fiscal current transfer is a financial example with no assumed production; it is not an investment grant. A procurement scenario would also require real delivery and cost/value-added accounts. CB secondary purchases transfer the existing bond; they supply no new proceeds to the Treasury. Public consolidation changes the form, not the outstanding amount, of public liabilities to the private sector in the purchase step.
